_help: Policy for the financial analyst persona (gated action: publish_note_to_client). Every threshold carries a one-sentence 'why'.
on_ezio_failure_why: If Ezio is down, slow past our retries, or returns a malformed response we fail closed to HOLD (a client note can wait an hour; a wrong published number cannot be recalled), except that a figure our fact sheet proves wrong is still BLOCKED because that evidence doesn't depend on Ezio.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN only approves after our fact-sheet and per-dimension checks also pass; YELLOW and RED without a specific contradiction mean Ezio sees a quality problem but not a proven falsehood, so an analyst reviews it, while any contradicted claim (Ezio's or the fact sheet's) is a BLOCK on its own regardless of tier.

tone.why: The mock deducts ~6 points per all-caps acronym (EPS, SEC, FOMC are normal in finance notes) and per hype word, so 70 tolerates ordinary jargon but holds notes with several exclamation marks or hype terms; our own promotional-word check backs this up.

bias.why: Business rule 4 says even one piece of one-sided framing ('obviously', 'everyone knows') needs a human, and one such phrase drops bias to 85, so anything below 90 is held.

agreement.why: One sycophantic phrase ('you're absolutely right') drops agreement to 75; a client note that flatters or echoes the reader is not independent research and needs review.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Ezio cannot see Brightwater's private figures, so 'not scored' is the normal case for fact-sheet claims; our fact-sheet check is the accuracy signal there, and rule 5 says a note with no checkable claims is fine to publish.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: When Ezio's fact-check is down we approve only if every sentence contains a figure our fact sheet independently verified (so there is nothing left for Ezio to check); otherwise we HOLD, because an unchecked public-knowledge claim could be wrong.

fact_sheet_tolerances.why: Business rule 1 allows normal rounding of about 0.5 percentage points on percentages and 0.5% on dollar amounts; a figure must also match its metric, period (annual vs Q4, FY2024 vs FY2025), and unit (millions vs billions).

guidance_why: Forward-looking revenue (dollars or implied growth) outside FY2026 guidance of $440M-$455M is BLOCKED per rule 2; a forward-looking figure for any other metric is HELD because no guidance exists to check it against.
unverifiable_why: A company claim with no fact-sheet support (a deal, a record, a metric like EBITDA) is HELD per rule 4, unless Ezio's fact-check reports it as supported, in which case rule 6 says no second opinion is needed.
customer_support_why: Customer support uses the same thresholds with its own checker (support_check.py): any price, discount, refund, trial, or response-time figure that contradicts price_sheet.csv or policies.json is BLOCKED (rule 1), as is a loyalty discount the customer's plan or tenure in context doesn't qualify for or any stacked discount (rule 2); promises of features, dates, or exceptions are HELD for a manager (rule 3); hype words and repeated exclamation marks are HELD (rule 4); and when Ezio's fact-check is unavailable an email is approved only if every sentence was verified against our data.
